correctness.rationale: For each real height h>0 the invariant affine-plane model must weight a direction by its full support width. From the five-vertex graph K5 minus the apex–apex edge, a generic separating plane cuts exactly k(5-k) minus one edge iff the two apices are separated, giving odd-section offset length 2h|z|. Direct normal integration yields total width 4D(h), odd-section measure 4πh, six-sided measure 12K(h) via the projected median, and three-sided measure 4[D(h)-C] by support-function gaps at the two degree-three apices. Complement gives the other section probabilities. Substitution/primitive checks agree with I,K definitions; the pentagon probability π(h+c)/D−1 has derivative sign Q=D−(h+c)D′, with Q′=−(h+c)D′′<0 and endpoint signs ±πc, proving one global maximum, not merely a finite optimum. Independent seeded 120000-direction edge-cut numerical sampling at h=.35,1.2114484,2.3 agreed with all four closed probabilities within 0.002; this only cross-checks, does not prove, the continuum formula.
residual_risks: No finite check replaces the analytic proof; claims quantified as in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: A five-vertex triangular bipyramid is a natural minimal nontrivial 3D polytope, and Euclidean-motion-invariant affine section probabilities require nonuniform directional weighting. The exact complete four-event law for every aspect ratio and rigid global maximizer solve a motivated natural shape statistic, with a substantive parity/edge-absence decomposition and a pentagon-optimal shape distinct from the equilateral-faced solid. This is not merely a possible-face-count table.
residual_risks: Value depends on precisely stated natural object and invariant; no general downstream theorem claimed.

limitations: Right symmetric equilateral-base bipyramids only; invariant affine-plane Crofton measure, not uniform central planes or skew bipyramids.
Numerical optimizer is approximate; strict uniqueness is analytical.
